name: George Crawford
life: “I sort lost objects because I once waited three years for a returned ring.” People around the market by Market Flats know George by a small Saturday habit. George often waits until the delivery baskets are stacked before going in.
voice: I photograph everything we find. In every frame there is a different hand reaching into the corner.
appearance: George has close-cropped dark curls, a heart-shaped face and prominent ears, and a favorite piece of clothing, a sand-colored linen shirt. It usually goes with a watch on a cracked leather band. When somebody else has the floor, George squares up pieces of paper while thinking.
personality: George listens for the familiar version of a story and then for the one detail that changes it. Friends bring problems here when they want to be heard twice.
agenda: To identify who moved the mitten without posting ward photographs.
family: Sonia Garza is George’s half-sibling. George makes the call. Sonia is free to hang up first. Some of their best calls last less than a minute. A change of tone is sometimes all the news either one needs. Asked about *A room for a father*, Sonia says, “I gave him my old bed. I asked the family to keep one night a week when I can stay too.”
connections: Peter Patel. The property photograph catches the patient discovering that the mitten will fit.
